info.name: Discord DMs & Moderation
info.description:
Every REST endpoint of both services, run top to bottom. The services read the caller from the identity headers in the communication contract (X-Player-Id, X-Session-Id, X-Session-Role, X-Record-Access) and never see a token on REST, so this collection sets those headers itself. Requests that leave them out act as a service-to-service call.

The first request generates fresh ids for the session, the moderator and a junior mod, so the collection can be re-run without clashes. Upstream services are mocked inside both services, which is what makes the access and outcome checks deterministic.

Start the stack (docker compose up -d dm-db dm-service moderation-db moderation-service). Discord DMs answers on 3002 and Moderation on 3003; change dmBaseUrl and moderationBaseUrl to run them standalone.

exec: // Fresh ids every run, so the collection can be re-run without clashes.
// The mocked Session access-check lets a junior mod into a channel when
// sha256(sessionId:playerId:channel) >= 0.2. Pick a junior mod with at least
// one allowed and one denied default channel, so both cases can be tested.
const ok = channels.filter((c) => allowed(v.get('sessionId'), j, c));
